body: Lost Kingdoms II is FromSoftware's GameCube action role-playing sequel, set generations after Katia's adventure. Tara, a member of a thieves' guild, carries a True Runestone that allows her to command magical cards. Her journey draws her into a struggle over the production and use of those stones, while the earlier heroine has become a figure of history. Real-time encounters again depend on the creatures and effects available in the deck. The player explores with a character whose immediate survival is tied to a collection prepared before the next danger appears.

New transformation cards allow Tara to take a creature's form, making the deck useful for movement and exploration as well as attacking an enemy. Returning cards receive revised effects, and enhanced uses can be purchased by spending more of the available resource. Particular combinations produce stronger results, encouraging the player to consider relationships between cards rather than evaluate each one alone. Areas can also be revisited after completion. A new card may change how a familiar route can be crossed or what can be accomplished during another visit.

Encounters take place within the explored environments, making movement through the level and the use of cards feel more closely connected. The new mechanical element sits beside fire, water, wood, earth and neutral, broadening the categories around which a collection can be developed. Kota Hoshino returned to compose the score. Released in 2003, the sequel's most useful change is to let a card alter the controlled character directly. The deck becomes more than assistance summoned nearby: it can determine what Tara herself is capable of becoming.
